text: When you design a REST API, you should follow some simple best practices. First, use clear and meaningful endpoints, such as /users or /orders, so developers can understand them easily. Second, always return the correct HTTP status codes, like 200 for success or 404 when a resource is not found. Good documentation is also essential, because it helps other developers learn how to use your API quickly. Finally, use versioning, for example /v1/users, so that older applications keep working when you make changes. These practices make your API easier to use, maintain, and trust.
